lines.en: Wow, a suitcase on your bed! **What are you going to do** this summer?
lines.pt: Uau, uma mala em cima da cama! O que você vai fazer neste verão?

lines.en: **I’m going to** visit my sister in Seattle. **I’m leaving** on July 3rd.
lines.pt: Vou visitar minha irmã em Seattle. Viajo no dia 3 de julho.

lines.en: Nice! **Are you going to** stay long?
lines.pt: Legal! Você vai ficar muito tempo?

lines.en: Two weeks. **We’re planning to** hike and visit the old market.
lines.pt: Duas semanas. Estamos planejando fazer trilhas e visitar o mercado antigo.

lines.en: That sounds great. **Are you going to** take your camera?
lines.pt: Parece ótimo. Você vai levar a sua câmera?

lines.en: Of course! And **I’m not going to** check email, I promise. I need a real break.
lines.pt: Claro! E não vou olhar e-mail, prometo. Preciso de uma pausa de verdade.

lines.en: Good idea. **I’m hoping to** go camping in August, but nothing is certain yet.
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Espero acampar em agosto, mas ainda não há nada certo.

lines.en: Then **you’re going to** need a tent! Mine is in the closet, take it.
lines.pt: Então você vai precisar de uma barraca! A minha está no armário, pode pegar.

lines.en: Really? Thanks! **I’m going to** pay you back with photos.
lines.pt: Sério? Obrigado! Vou retribuir com fotos.

pages.title: Talking About Your Plans

situation.text: A friend is packing for a trip. You ask about the plans, talk about your own plans and offer help. You say what you are going to do, what is decided and what is only a hope.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can talk about plans and intentions, ask about a friend’s plans and say what is decided or only hoped.
canDo: Say a plan: I’m going to…
Ask about plans: What are you going to do?
Say a shared plan: We’re planning to…
Say what is not certain: I’m hoping to…
success: I say what I am going to do.
I ask about my friend’s plans.
I say one thing that is not certain.
pages.think: In Portuguese you can say “vou viajar” or “estou pensando em viajar”. How do you show in English that a plan is decided or just an idea?

teach.goal: Abrir a aula pela situação real, não pela regra.
solo: Leia o objetivo e peça que o estudante diga, com as próprias palavras, o que vai conseguir fazer hoje.
Faça a pergunta “Think about it” antes de mostrar qualquer expressão.
group: Cada estudante diz uma palavra ou ideia que associa à situação.
Mostre os critérios de sucesso: eles são a missão final da aula.
support: Aceite respostas curtas ou em português na primeira rodada e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about the student’s life, not a grammar test.
intro.group: One question per student, then a follow-up question to a classmate.

pages.recall: Advice: “You should… / Why don’t you…?”. Ask: What advice would you give a friend who is going on a long trip?

qs.q: What are you going to do after class today?
qs.pt: O que você vai fazer depois da aula hoje?
sup: I’m going to see a friend.

qs.q: Do you have any plans for the weekend?
qs.pt: Você tem planos para o fim de semana?

qs.q: Where would you like to travel next?
qs.pt: Para onde você gostaria de viajar a seguir?

pages.tip: Use the answers to find gaps and to recycle earlier content. The goal is to enter English from the first minute.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma no primeiro minuto e mapear lacunas.
extra: What are you going to cook this week?
Where would you like to live in ten years?

errors.w: Tomorrow I go to the doctor (plano)
errors.r: Tomorrow I’m going to the doctor.

support: Ofereça as respostas-modelo (chips) e peça apenas que escolham uma e a ampliem com um motivo.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Talking about future plans
pages.intro: In the USA, people often share plans in a relaxed way and mark how sure they are: “I’m going to…” for decided plans and “I’m hoping to…” for ideas. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: A wish. It is not certain yet.
A shared plan that is being organized.

qs.q: How do people say a plan is not certain?
qs.pt: Como dizer que um plano não é certo?

levels.B1: They use I’m hoping to…, I might… or Nothing is set in stone.
levels.B2: Hedging expressions such as I’m hoping to or We’ll see signal that the plan can change, which avoids disappointing others.

qs.q: Why do people ask “What are you up to this weekend?”
qs.pt: Por que perguntam “What are you up to this weekend?”

levels.A2: It is a friendly question about plans.
levels.B1: It is common small talk and can lead to an invitation.
levels.B2: It is a typical opener; sometimes it is a way to invite you, so it is wise to reply with a detail and a question back.

qs.q: Is “We should hang out sometime” a real invitation?
qs.pt: “We should hang out sometime” é um convite de verdade?

levels.B1: It can be vague; a real invitation has a day or time.
levels.B2: Without a day or a time it may be just friendly talk, so make it concrete with Are you free on Saturday?

pages.compare: In Brazil “a gente se fala” or “vamos marcar” is also often a polite phrase. In the USA a real plan usually has a day and a time. Does that happen where you live?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto cultural e as primeiras hipóteses.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses antes de explicar.
Peça que compare com o que acontece no Brasil.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica em uma frase.
Pergunte “Do you agree?” entre colegas.
answers: Q1: I’m hoping to / I might / nothing is set in stone.
Q2: pergunta simpática; pode virar convite.
Q3: sem dia e hora costuma ser só gentileza.
extra: How do you invite a friend for a real plan?
Have you ever received a vague invitation?
support: Use as respostas de nível A1 como andaime e peça que repitam.
stretch: B2: compare o registro e o tom entre Brasil e EUA com exemplos reais.

pass1.q: Why does Maya have a suitcase on her bed?
pass1.pt: Por que a Maya tem uma mala na cama?
opts: She is going on a trip

teach.goal: Compreender a situação antes de ver o texto: ideia principal e depois informações específicas.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: só a ideia principal.
2ª escuta: peça os detalhes pedidos nas tarefas. Só depois mostre o texto.
group: Escuta coletiva; duplas anotam antes de revelar.
Compare as respostas entre duplas e só então mostre o texto.
answers: Pass 1: She is going on a trip
Pass 2: Seattle · July 3rd · two weeks · hike · camping
extra: Which plans are certain and which are only hopes?
How does Maya feel about the trip?
support: Pause depois de cada fala se necessário.

qs.q: Who does Maya want to visit?
What is Maya not going to do?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: O estudante lê um papel e você lê o outro; depois troquem.
Peça que reconte a conversa no nível que conseguir.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia: uma frase por estudante.
answers: Her sister · Two weeks · Check email · Her tent
extra: What would YOU do in Seattle?
What other question would you ask Maya?

errors.w: What you are going to do?
errors.r: What are you going to do?

support: Mostre a tradução (botão PT) depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.en: What are you going to do?

items.use: Say a plan with other people.
Say a wish that is not certain.
Say what you decided not to do.
Say a fixed time or date.
Say that the plan can change.

items.en: What are you going to do this summer?
I’m going to visit my sister.
I’m not going to check email.

pages.note: Instead of memorizing the whole list, choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again. The others are for understanding and for stretching later.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks para uso repetido e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?” antes de dar o significado.
Compare formal × informal e peça um exemplo próprio.
group: Cada estudante escolhe a expressão que mais usaria e explica quando.
Comparem equivalentes em duplas.
answers: Asking about plans · Decided plan · Shared plan · Uncertain plan · Negative plan
extra: Which expression would you use for a sure plan?
How can you say a plan may change?
support: Trabalhe só as expressões ★ nesta aula.

patterns.name: Plans with going to
ex: I’m going to visit my sister.

patterns.name: Questions
ex: Are you going to stay long?
Are you going to take your camera?
What are you going to do?

patterns.name: Negative plans
patterns.formula: Subject + **be not going to** + base verb
ex: I’m not going to check email.

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: I am going to visit my sister.
We are considering a camping trip.
I do not intend to check email.
Would you like to join us?
register.note: Gonna is normal in speech and informal messages, but in formal writing use going to.

teach.goal: Fixar os padrões principais (01 e 02); os outros são expansão. Usar a troca de palavras para variar a fala.
solo: Mostre o padrão DENTRO do diálogo (grife os chunks).
Use “Swap the words”: toque em cada peça e peça que o estudante diga a frase completa.
Compare spoken × written em 2 exemplos.
group: Troca em cadeia: cada estudante muda UMA peça e o próximo repete a frase.
Em pares: um escolhe as peças, o outro fala.
teach.answers: Padrões 01 e 02 são o foco; 03 e 04 são expansão para quem avançar rápido.
extra: Change a plan into a question.
support: Fique só com o padrão 01 na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combine dois padrões na mesma resposta.

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: In fast speech, going to becomes “gonna” /ˈɡʌnə/. You can use it with friends, but in writing and formal speech say going to. Stress the main verb: I’m gonna VISit.

items.say: I’m going to visit my sister.
What are you going to do?

opts: What are you going to do?
identify.say: What are you going to do?

own.prompt: Write a true plan for next month with going to.
own.criteria: Say it twice: once with going to, once with gonna. Did you stress the verb?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno de pronúncia: Reduction: going to → gonna.
solo: 3 passagens: escutar e identificar, reproduzir ritmo e entonação, usar em frase com conteúdo próprio.
Modele devagar e em velocidade normal; peça que bata palmas na sílaba forte.
group: Coro, depois duplas; circule ouvindo.
Cada estudante cria uma frase própria usando o fenômeno.
answers: Identify: I’m gonna go. · What are you going to do?
extra: In which situation is gonna not appropriate?
support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas em voz alta.

items.q: 3. Your plan is only a hope.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado: escolher, completar, substituir e responder antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que o estudante justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça uma versão mais informal ou mais educada.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem antes de revelar.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: I’m going to visit my sister. · What are you going to do? · I’m hoping to go camping. · I’m not going to check email. · is · planning · Are you going to stay long? · I’m not going to work on Sunday. · I’m going to visit my family and rest.
extra: Say each correct answer fast, with gonna, and slowly, with going to.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — talk about your plans

brief.teacher: You are a curious friend. Ask about plans and add a surprising detail or problem.
brief.student: You are the friend with plans: say what you are going to do, what is certain and what is only an idea.

complications: Your friend asks for exact dates: answer or say it is not certain.
A problem appears: the plan may change.
Your friend wants to join: respond.
You don’t know a word: explain it another way.

rounds.label: With support
help: What are you going to do?

success: I say what I am going to do.
I ask about my friend’s plans.
I say one thing that is not certain.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação inesperada e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Combine o cenário com a vida real do estudante.
Rodada 1: com chunks. Rodada 2: só palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Meta de fala: 60–70% do tempo para o estudante. Anote 2–3 correções para a devolutiva.
extra: What if your friend wants to change your plan?

errors.w: I go to travel next month.
errors.r: I’m going to travel next month.

support: Volte à rodada 1 se travar; peça que repita só a primeira frase.
stretch: Acrescente uma segunda complicação no meio da cena.

rounds.title: My plans
rounds.task: Tell your partner three plans for next month.
rounds.hint: I’m going to… / We’re planning to…

rounds.title: Ask more
rounds.task: Ask your partner three questions about their plans.

rounds.title: Not certain
rounds.task: Say one decided plan, one hope and one thing you are not going to do.
rounds.hint: I’m hoping to… / I’m not going to…

rounds.title: Compare
rounds.task: Whole group: find one plan that two people share.

infogap.title: Weekend plans
infogap.instr: Ask your partner and complete your card. Do not look at the other card!

a.title: Card A: Maya’s plans
a.task: You know Maya’s trip. Ask about Ben’s plans.

b.title: Card B: Ben’s plans
b.task: You know Ben’s trip. Ask about Maya’s plans.

teach.goal: Fluência por repetição da função com informações novas a cada rodada.
group: Troque os pares a cada rodada (A+B / C+D → A+C / B+D → A+D / B+C → grupo todo).
Responsabilidade individual: cada aluno faz ≥1 pergunta e ≥1 resposta.
Circule anotando 2–3 correções prioritárias.
answers: A: Maya, Seattle · hiking. B: Ben, lake in Maine · camping and fishing. Perguntas: Where is she going to go? What is he going to do?
support: Entregue frases-modelo no chat da turma.

pages.title: Group mission — plan your future
pages.goal: Each group must exchange real plans, ask follow-up questions and decide one thing to do together.

missions.mission: Plan a day trip together: where, when and what you are going to take.
missions.constraint: Use “We’re planning to…” and “Are you going to…?”
missions.start: What are you going to do on Saturday?

missions.mission: Talk about goals for the next year. One of them has a big plan and the other asks about details.
missions.constraint: Use “I’m hoping to…” and “I’m going to…”
missions.start: What are your plans for next year?

missions.mission: Plan a small party at home: who is going to do what.
missions.constraint: Use “I’m going to…” and “I’m not going to…” once each.
missions.start: We’re going to have a party. What are you going to do?

success: I say what I am going to do.
I ask about my friend’s plans.
I say one thing that is not certain.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: o objetivo é resolver, não só falar certo.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão. Alterne os papéis.
Progressão: 1ª rodada com frases de apoio, 2ª só palavras-chave, 3ª sem roteiro.
Observe e anote 2–3 correções prioritárias; devolutiva no fim.
answers: Modelo: “What are you going to do this summer?” → “I’m going to visit my sister.” → “Are you going to stay long?” → “Two weeks. We’re planning to hike.”
support: Dê o início de frase (“Start with”) em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a friend about your plans for the next vacation or weekend: one decided plan, one hope and one thing you are not going to do.
pages.model: Hi Ben! **I’m going to** visit my sister in Seattle on July 3rd. **We’re planning to** hike and go to the market. **I’m hoping to** see the ocean too. **I’m not going to** check email, I promise! **What are you going to do** this summer?
checklist: I used going to for a decided plan.
I used planning to or hoping to.
I asked a question about my friend’s plans.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea instead of rewriting everything.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação comunicativa.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários e mostre uma forma mais natural.
group: Cada estudante escreve; depois troquem os textos e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add one more plan with a date.
support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar os dados.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You said what is decided and what is only a hope.
prompts.improve: Example: Do not forget be before going to (I’m going to, not I going to).
prompts.next: Example: Make a plan with a friend, with a date and a time.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

items: Record a 45–60 second audio about your plans for next month.
Write five sentences: three decided plans and two hopes.
Ask a friend about their plans in English by message.
Listen to the dialogue again and mark every future form.

unit: Tell · describe · compare · book · opine · advise · plan

teach.goal: Toda aula termina com uma produção observável.
solo: Sem consultar as anotações: construir uma pergunta, responder a uma situação e usar uma expressão nova.
group: Exit challenge individual; compare com o colega e combine a tarefa de continuidade.
answers: What are you going to do this summer? · Yes, I’m going to stay for a week. · I’m hoping to go camping, but nothing is certain.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: I go to the beach tomorrow.
ladder.goal: Say a simple future with models.

ladder.say: I’m going to visit my sister, and we’re planning to hike.
I’m hoping to take two weeks off, if my manager agrees.
Provided that the flights are reasonable, we’re thinking of extending the trip.
We’ve loosely mapped out an itinerary, but we’d like to leave room for spontaneity.
Rather than fix every detail, we intend to let the journey suggest its own course.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
extra: Which sentence would you like to be able to say next month?
